THE COMPLETE COLLECTION

All 275 restaurants

Menus, dates, fees and the details behind each listing.+

Alphabetical census of every published listing. “Native” means PDF text, “OCR” means image text recognition, “visual” means original page image inspected, “partial” means some price/grouping/portion details remain unresolved, and “missing” means actual event dishes unavailable. Source links point to the live official listing; that page carries menu links and directions. Unknown service charges are not assumed absent. Published SRW hours may differ from regular opening hours; the menu’s narrower restrictions prevail.

THE NOTEBOOKResearch notes+
Service-charge update: Kamonegi also applies a 20% service charge: its $65 menu is $78 before tax. Price bars compare base food prices, not all-in bills. This page preserves the October 25, 2026 research; bookings and availability are not guaranteed.

Search all restaurants · Download all275 menus(CSV)
On phones, swipe tables horizontally; restaurant names stay visible.

Fall 2026 · October 18–31 · Checked October 25, 2026 · Seattle and the wider participating region

Rankings use documented signature-menu overlap and sourced prices. The same scoring and evidence criteria apply across the full restaurant census.

Scope: 275 published listings, each with an audit row. Menu sources located for273; FORTUNA and Seattle Bento Pops have no verified event dishes. “Located” is not the same as fully interpreted: partial/ambiguous entries remain marked in the appendix. Branches are separate rows, including chains. Ordinary-menu percentage savings and current reservation availability were not comprehensively verified.

Price rule: Headline amounts are published event food/package prices, not all-in bills. Tax, optional drinks, gratuity or mandatory service may apply. “For two” is explicitly normalized. Unknown fees are not zero.

Menu restrictions and price caveats

  • $65 can mean $78 before tax: Shiro’s, Aerlume, AQUA/El Gaucho, Seastar and L’Oursin disclose20% service. Staple & Fancy discloses22%: $65 becomes$79.30 before tax. These charges are not automatically a reason to add another full tip; read each policy.
  • El Gaucho Bellevue is not a filet-mignon deal: its event steak is top-sirloin culotte; lobster medallions add$25. Seattle’s menu is different and offers short rib. Do not transfer dishes across branches.
  • Generic expensive three-course sets are not automatic bargains: prioritize a distinctive signature dish, multiple substantive preparations or an explicit share package. No verified ordinary-menu discount percentage is asserted here.
  • BUBU is time-sensitive: onlyOct26–27 remain, walk-ins5–9pm. L’Oursin’s menu specifically saysOct26–28, overriding the broader directory schedule. Joule’s remaining offer runsOct25–29. Ramen Nori isMon–Thuonly.
  • Whole-table participation: La Mar, MariPili, L’Oursin and some hot-pot sets require the table to use the event menu. Supplements, portion sizes, dietary restrictions and branch-specific hours are in the appendix.

Method, coverage and limits

The official WordPress restaurant directory was paged in full and deduplicated by post ID, with275 asserted records. Every detail page was fetched, menu assets downloaded, PDFs text-extracted or OCR’d, and menu summaries audited in three disjoint batches. A parent pass checked high-impact layout/price traps against images, recovered Unicode asset URLs, and used a dated first-party announcement for both Reuben’s taprooms. Final IDs and CSV rows were asserted in code.

411 Cedar St, Seattle, WA 98121  |  wazseattle.com


WHAT IS OCHAZUKE?
Ochazuke is a familiar Japanese comfort dish of rice enjoyed in stages, finished with hot tea or dashi. At
BUBU, the toppings and condiments let each bowl change as you eat.
HOW TO ENJOY BUBU
1
Taste it first
2
Add condiments
3
Add nori and more
4
Pour over the hot dashi and enjoy as ochazuke.
Taste it in stages. Make it your own.

The Story Behind Our Name
Named for one of golf’s most storied traditions, the Calcutta auction celebrates the spirit of friendly 
competition, camaraderie, and the shared excitement of the game.
Inspired by that same spirit, The Calcutta Grill is a place to gather, celebrate, and enjoy good food in 
great company. Rooted in the traditions of golf, yet welcoming to all, we invite you to experience the 
timeless pleasures of gracious hospitality and the extraordinary beauty of the Pacific Northwest.

Nibby Toast  (vegan)
Toasted baguette topped with whipped tofu spread, candied cocoa nibs, 
raspberry, and panela syrup (Vegan), with a house-made fruit jam using cacao 
fruit pulp.
 
Cucumber Salad  (vegan, gluten free)
Sliced cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, and cocoa nibs in a sesame dressing.
Chickpea Salad Wrap w/ Chips (vegan)
Cocoa nib chickpea salad made with vegan mayo, served in a tortilla wrap with 
sliced cucumbers. Served with a side of chips.
 
Beet and Sweet Potato Autumn Salad (vegan, gluten free)
Spinach salad topped with roasted beets and sweet potatoes, red onion, and 
candied cocoa nib & pepita clusters. Served with cocoa nib infused vinaigrette. 
Coffee Cake (vegan)
Coffee cake studded with chocolate chunks and topped with cocoa nib streusel. 
 
Chocolate Con Queso 
Our take on a traditional Colombian dish. A piece of Quesillo Oaxaca cheese 
dropped into a rich sipping chocolate for a cheesy, melty delight.  Served with a 
vegan shortbread cookie for dipping.
Curated by Chef Katy Fuller. 
Pick one plate from each section, for $35.

Forum Cheeseburger
A half pound of Royal Ranch ground beef topped with american cheese
and served on a brioche bun with shredded lettuce, tomato, onion,
house-made pickles and topped with our signature Forum aioli
Black Bean “Burger”
A spicy, southwestern vegan burger made with a savory blend of black
beans, brown rice, corn, diced tomatoes, and green and red peppers
served on a vegan brioche bun with our secret recipe vegan chipotle
aioli, and lettuce and pico de gallo.
BBQ Chicken Sando
Slow braised BBQ pulled chicken on a brioche bun with house-made
pickles and crispy fried shaved onions and jalapeños for crunch
Proper Chicken and Waffles
Our secret recipe sweet 'n' spiced waffles paired with two large chicken
tenders, topped with our chili honey butter, powdered sugar, chopped
scallions. House-made jalapeño maple glaze served on the side
MAINS
PICK ONE
THREE COURSE EXPERIENCE | $35 PER PERSON
TASTINGS
PICK ONE
Classic Caesar Salad
Traditional style caesar salad with chopped romaine tossed in
house-made caesar dressing and topped with house-made garlic
croutons and parmesan
Pulled Chicken Quesadilla
A crispy, flakey flour tortilla stuffed with savory slow braised
chicken thigh and melted jack and cheddar cheeses. Lime crema
and house-made roasted salsa on the side
Crispy Brussels Sprouts
Crispy fried brussels sprouts tossed in a chili maple glaze with bacon,
jalapeños, and parmesan cheese
DESSERTS
PICK ONE
Guinness Chocolate Cake
Chocolate and Guinness. House-made with Guinness irish stout
and a cream cheese frosting separating layers of a rich and moist
chocolate cake. Worth saving room for!
Brown Butter Cake
Brown butter cake topped with cream cheese frosting, toasted
almonds, basil chiffonade with apricot purée and candied orange
zest

FIRST COURSE: 
• 
Arugula Strawberry Salad (V) 
o 
Arugula, strawberries, walnuts & gorgonzola, tossed with balsamic vinaigrette. 
• 
Caesar Salad (V) 
o 
Crisp, hand cut romaine with classic Caesar dressing, shredded parmesan and crisp croutons. 
• 
Gamberoni Pistachio 
o 
Jumbo prawns sautéed with garlic and brandy in pistachio-spinach pesto, served over a bed of 
fresh spinach. 
• 
Vongole e Cozze 
o 
Fresh clams & mussels steamed in white wine, garlic, olive oil, butter, crushed red pepper flakes, 
and Italian parsley. 
 
SECOND COURSE: 
• 
Pollo Piccata 
o

• 
Pollo Marsala 
o

or spaghetti. 
• 
Rigatoni Boscaiola 
o 
Rigatoni with Italian plum tomato meat sauce with sweet peas, mushrooms and a touch of cream. 
• 
Spaghetti al Porro (V) 
o

parmesan. 
• 
Spaghetti Carbonara 
o 
Spaghetti, pancetta, egg yolk, pecorino cheese & black pepper.

*we kindly decline any modifications or substitutions for our Tapear Tapearei menu and require full table
participation during Seattle Restaurant Week


DESAYUNO
On Sundays after church Abuela would serve us a huge spread, catering to all of our different tastes. While Abuela 
prepared the meal, Abuelo would putter around. At the end of the meal Abuelo would tell us all of his childhood 
silly stories when he was in the Pyrenees in Spain. His blue eyes would light up when he recalled what a menace he 
was, stealing eggs from his neighbors, throwing snowballs down their chimneys, and shooting his friends with milk 
straight from a sheep’s udder. Abuela typically sat there quietly, halfway listening, smiling at each of her grandkids.
COMIDA
Lunch was the principal meal every day except Sunday and usually comprised of many dishes like stewed lentils with 
pork, huge cazuelas with paella, green salad, cutlets, meatballs, not to mention special dishes like squid in ink just for 
me and pig’s feet for my dad. During and after the meal Abuela loved to sip on cheap rose while Abuelo warmed up 
his storytelling again. Often at this point he would bring up all of his experiences as a shepherd from the gruelling 
conditions to the eventual golden tickets of a shepherd’s visa to come to the United States to work where he would 
eventually meet my Abuela.
MERIENDA
 When I think of the mid-afternoon treats Abuela would make for us, I remember summertime. She would deliver 
chicken empanada when I was stuck all day in a tractor working, or bring out sweets with fruit or almonds when 
we were all enjoying time in her garden. This was the special alone time we had together while Abuelo was napping. 
During this afternoon time, she would be preparing for dinner already and would tell her own stories of how 
wonderful her daughter MariPili was who she missed dearly.
CENA 
During summertime, we often grilled lamb chops on the patio, marinated with garlic, parsley, olive oil, and black 
pepper. Abuelo, my siblings, and I raised the lamb ourselves and the quality was unbeatable. Abuela would serve it 
simply with a green vegetable and potatoes. My Abuelo loved to brag about Abuela, talking about how she cooked 
for Robert Finch in Los Angeles, how she laboriously worked on the farm, how she sacrificed and left MariPili in 
Spain to support her family. He always said no matter how hard his life sounded through his stories, hers was harder. 
She would grit her teeth and give a single nod.
SOBREMESA: Time at Abuela’s dining table
Sobremesa is an integral part of the Spaniard’s life, relaxing at the table after a meal. My Abuelo and Abuela 
instilled this tradition in me at their home. We grew up on a farm in Eastern Washington started by my 
Abuelos after they emigrated from Spain, later carried on by my father. My Abuela delighted in making 
multi-course meals, while my Abuelo relished in the post meal-induced coma that provided him a captive 
audience. 
POSTRE
Dessert often was served twice a day due to Abuela’s sweet tooth. Both of my abuelos loved the fruit the Columbia 
Basin had to offer that their friends would bring them fresh-picked by the case. Abuela loved to serve a fruit salad 
with a splash of brandy, swiss rolls, cheesecake, rice pudding, and more. My abuelos would come together in their 
storytelling when they were reminiscing on their kids and grandchildren’s younger selves. They cherished their time 
with us as much as we did with them, and the Sobremesa I had shared with them is the reason MariPili Tapas Bar 
exists!
